prompt: A sensor logs the temperature $T(t)$ of a cooling drink, in degrees Celsius, but it dropped the reading at exactly $t = 5$ minutes. Nearby it recorded $T(4.9) = 61.2$, $T(4.99) = 60.12$, $T(5.01) = 59.88$, $T(5.1) = 58.8$. What does $\lim_{t \to 5} T(t)$ appear to be?
hint: The missing reading does not matter. A limit only asks where the readings are heading as $t$ closes in on $5$.

hints.text: The missing reading does not matter. A limit only asks where the readings are heading as $t$ closes in on $5$.
From before $t = 5$: $61.2$, then $60.12$. From after: $58.8$, then $59.88$. Both are closing in on the same temperature.
Both sides head to $60$, so $\lim_{t \to 5} T(t) = 60$ degrees.

explanation: From the left the readings fall: $61.2 \to 60.12$, getting close to $60$.
From the right the readings rise: $58.8 \to 59.88$, also getting close to $60$.
The two sides agree, so the limit is $60$. The drink was almost surely at $60$ degrees at $t = 5$, even though the sensor missed it.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fill in the gap like a detective
steps: Each step ten times closer in time brings the reading ten times closer: $1.2$ away, then $0.12$ away.
Continue the pattern: $0.012$ away, $0.0012$ away, and so on toward $60$.
The sensor dropped one point, but the pattern tells you exactly what it would have said.
